newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore jet fuel edges up amid regional demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore jet fuel edges up amid regional demand.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel rose slightly on Monday as tight supplies faced fresh demand from the Indian subcontinent and North Asian, while the other products held steady in dull trade as Japan entered a week-long holiday, industry sources said.
The January jet fuel/gas oil swaps spread strengthened and was last quoted at $2.30/$2.50 per barrel, up from Friday's $2.00/$2.50.
A trader bid for 100,000-barrels of jet fuel loading in mid-January at $33.75 a barrel free-on-board Singapore but no sellers emerged.
Traders said the fresh demand came on top of the issue of purchase tenders for jet fuel and gas oil last week by India, Nepal and Sri Lanka.

Gas oil was steady amid expectations for a new wave of Chinese purchases for end January and February arrival cargoes. Traders expect China's January purchases to equal the estimated 800,000 tonnes it imported for December. Currently, China is bidding around $255 per tonne cost-and-freight south China, $2-3 higher than last week's bid, one trader said.
Two majors each sold 150,000 barrels of gas oil each to a Thai and a Kuwaiti trader at $32.50 a barrel for January 14-18.

Gasoline and naphtha were quiet ahead of the close of Taiwan's buy tenders on Monday. Some traders expected firm offers in the reformate tender, citing the absence of Thai exports cargoes. But more bearish traders saw no additional demand for Singapore barrels from Australia due to the delay in the return of a 50,000 barrel-per-day cracker. Although stocks were depleted, sources said domestic supplies were sufficient. Chinese supplies were also ample amid low domestic and South Korean demand, the usual outlet for Chinese barrels.
